phase_3_disruption.declared: the driver emptied both fuel inventories and wrote nothing else

addressed_actions.what_changed: The model may add a `target` naming a visible handle to any action whose catalog template binds `$target`. The verb, item and count stay the discrete action's; only the addressee changes, so this grants addressing rather than a new capability.

before.failure: the agent fuelled whichever machine it was nearest, repeatedly: 47-48 coal into the drill and none into the furnace in three runs, 50 into the furnace and none into the drill in another

after.note: Commission reached both machines in four decisions -- give_coal_20 at h1, then at h2 -- and recovery took three. Token cost fell from 117,085 to 17,357 because the agent stopped walking back and forth trying to make 'nearest' mean the machine it wanted.

addressed_actions.a_bug_this_found: The first run with addressing enabled still failed, and the trace said why: 50 replies naming a target were refused as `unknown_target`. The demonstration driver had reimplemented the loop's stepping and never passed the addressable set, so it measured a feature it had switched off. It calls the loop's own helpers now.

withdrawal.traces_unchanged: Every other key in this file is the original run, byte for byte. What is withdrawn is the acceptance claim drawn from it, not the measurement.
why: No outage was ever established. The disruption emptied both fuel *inventories* at tick 4050 with `get_fuel_inventory():clear()`, which does not touch `entity.energy`, and this file's own `phase_3_disruption.state_after` records `drill_status: 1` -- working -- with `drill_fuel: 0`.

The line could not have stopped in the time available. `docs/evidence/r4-burner-decay.json` measured the decay curve on this same scene: production continued for 1,170 ticks after the fuel was taken, and the arithmetic agrees -- 2,999,833 J of remaining burning fuel against a 150 kW drill is 1,199 ticks. `phase_4_recovery` took 3 decisions, which is 90 ticks. The agent refuelled a line that was still running at full rate.

There was no criterion to judge either state by. `fuel == 0` is not an outage, and machine status is worse: a healthy plate line reads `working` on 7.5% of sampled ticks. `src/factoriorl/recovery.py` now declares both criteria, in code, before any arm runs.
There was no control arm, so nothing distinguished 'the agent restored the line' from 'the line never stopped'. Under the declared criteria the second is what happened.
replaced_by: docs/evidence/r4-burner-decay.json -- the decay curve this claim needed and did not have.
docs/evidence/r4-recovery-arms.json -- three arms from a digest-validated common pre-intervention state, with the agent arm repeated.
withdrawal.note: This file's `addressed_actions` block records that the model used *targeted* transfers here -- `give_coal_20` at h1, then at h2. R4.2's arms run the same task's declared catalog untargeted, where `give_coal_N` fuels whichever machine is nearest. That is a difference in what the agent could express, not in the task, and it is why the arm numbers are reported per run with a range rather than as one figure.
